name: Naturalisation (Barbados Citizenship Act, Cap. 186)

requirements.blocker_text: Requires 12 months of continuous residence in Barbados immediately preceding the date of application.
requirements.fix_path: Establish 12 months' continuous residence immediately before applying.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires at least 5 years' residence in Barbados in aggregate within the 7 years immediately preceding the date of application.
requirements.fix_path: Accumulate at least 5 years of residence within the relevant 7-year window.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires being of good character, assessed at the Minister's discretion, and an intention to reside in Barbados upon naturalisation.

evidence_required.document: Proof of continuous and aggregate residence (immigration records, permanent residence documentation)

sources.title: Barbados Judiciary (barbadoslawcourts.gov.bb) -- Barbados Citizenship Act, Cap. 186, Second Schedule

notes: NEW ROUTE, part of Barbados' initial build. prerequisites is null rather than requiring bb_permanent_residence first: the Citizenship Act's Second Schedule tests residence and character directly and does not state that formal Permanent Resident status must be held first -- bb_permanent_residence's switchable_to listing this route describes a plausible real path, not a confirmed legal requirement to go through PR first. dual_citizenship_allowed is left null rather than guessed -- not confirmed against a tier-1 source in this pass (several tier-3 guides claim Barbados permits dual citizenship broadly, not independently verified here). UPDATE (gap-fill pass): the original build of this route found NO descent-based or marriage-based citizenship provision in the Cap. 186 text extracted from barbadoslawcourts.gov.bb, and flagged this as a surprising, likely-outdated gap. That gap is now RESOLVED: the Immigration Department's own citizenship page (immigration.gov.bb/pages/Citizenship.aspx) -- a different tier-1 source, using different section numbering (3, 3(3), 3A(1)(b), 4(3), 5(1), 6) than the Second Schedule cited here -- plainly describes both grounds, now modelled as bb_citizenship_descent (Section 5(1)) and bb_citizenship_marriage (Sections 3(1), 3(3), 3A(1)(b), 6). The section-numbering mismatch between the two tier-1 sources confirms the original suspicion that the barbadoslawcourts.gov.bb consolidation of Cap. 186 may be out of date relative to a later amendment -- flagged, not silently reconciled; this bb_naturalisation route itself (residence-based naturalisation) may also sit under different section numbers in the more current version, not re-verified in this pass. dual_citizenship_allowed remains the one still-open question from the original build.
